institution: Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology (Deemed to be University), Chennai
disclaimer: Compiled from the institute's published regulation and curriculum PDFs, accessed 2026-10-12. Credits and marks are copied from the curriculum tables (L-T-P-C and CAE/ESE columns) and machine-checked against each semester's published credit total. The official grade sheet is authoritative.

2019.appliesTo: Students admitted 2019-20 to 2022-23 (course codes with 'A' after the programme code, e.g. SCSA1201, SMTA1101, S11APT1). Also the CSE specialisations whose 2021 curricula are published under the 2019 regulations.

specialGrades.meaning: Reappear: total 0-49. By inference also any failure of the 30% end-semester minimum, since that is a fail; the regulations do not name the grade for that case

pass.notes: 'A candidate should secure not less than 50% of total marks prescribed for the courses, subject to securing a minimum of 30% marks out of maximum mark in end semester exams.' Theory ESE is written for 100 and converted to 50, so the minimum is 30/100 raw = 15/50 converted; a 50-mark practical ESE needs 15/50. Applying 30% to a 25-mark ESE (1-credit labs) gives 7.5 - inferred, the regulations do not give that number.

2019.gpaRule: GPA = sum(Ci x GPi) / sum(Ci) over the courses successfully cleared in the semester; CGPA uses the same formula over all courses cleared in all semesters. Ci = course credits, GPi = grade point. RA, AAA, W and ABS are excluded from both numerator and denominator (a failed course does not pull the GPA down; it simply does not count until it is cleared). Non-credit courses (C = 0) contribute nothing. Grades are awarded on the course total out of 100.
2019.arrears: A failed course must be re-registered and the end-semester exam rewritten until it is passed (no limit on attempts). Continuous-assessment marks from the first appearance are retained for all later attempts. The regulations do not cap the grade of a later attempt and do not say in which semester's GPA a later pass is counted; CGPA counts every cleared course once.

internalComposition.theory: Two CAEs of 50 each. Total out of 100 converted to 40 + 10 marks (assignment in the UG Academic Regulations 2019 document; attendance % in the CSE-specialisation and M.E. 2019 editions) = 50. The earliest CSE 2019 edition says 45 (CAE) + 5 (attendance). Every version totals 50 internal.
internalComposition.practical: 25 continuous evaluation (experiments, observation, record) + 20 model exam + 5 attendance = 50 internal; end-semester practical exam 50. (The UG Academic Regulations 2019 evaluation-scheme table instead shows Record 30 + Model 20.)
internalComposition.project: 3 reviews (5 + 15 + 30) = 50 internal; final viva voce 50 (internal and external examiners 20 each + report 10).

Professional Training and Skill Enhancement are 100% external (30 of 100 needed). Mandatory Audit Courses: no ESE and no credits; PASS needs 80% attendance and 50% in the LMS assignments (cl. 22.3).

internalComposition.theory: CAE1 (50) + CAE2 (50) converted to 40, + assignment 10 = 50 internal; ESE 100 converted to 50.
internalComposition.practical: Continuous session-wise assessment 30 + model practical (50 converted to 20) = 50 internal; end-semester practical exam 50.
internalComposition.practicalHeavy: CAE (converted to 40) + assignment 10 = 50 internal; end-semester PRACTICAL exam 50 external.
internalComposition.theoryWithPbla: CAE (40) + assignment (10) = 50 internal; review/project report 50 external.
internalComposition.mandatoryAudit: Internal only (test marks 50); PASS/FAIL, no credits, no ESE.

2023.courseCodeFormat: S + programme code (2 letters, e.g. CS, IT, MT maths, PH physics, CY chemistry, HS english; numeric for courses with a practical or project component, e.g. CS = 11, IT = 12) + 'B' (Regulations 2023) + optional course type ('LH' practical-heavy theory, 'PB' project-based learning) + semester digit + sequence. Theory and practical courses use a four-digit numeric sequence (cl. 5.5 figure).

theory.notes: Both regulations. ESE written for 100 and converted to 50.

variants.when: 1-credit lab (L-T-P 0-0-2), e.g. Physics Lab, Chemistry Lab, Code Optimization and Debugging, Business Communication Lab

practical.notes: 2-credit labs (0-0-4) are 50 + 50 = 100. Most 1-credit labs are 25 + 25 = 50 (curriculum marks columns, semester mark totals and syllabus headers 'Total Marks 50' agree), but some 1-credit labs are 50 + 50 (e.g. SCSA2305, SCSA2401, SCSA2406, SCSA2407, SITA2301), so use the catalog entry when there is one. Grade bands are defined on marks out of 100, so a 50-mark lab total must be scaled to a percentage first.

integrated.notes: Regulations 2023 'Theory + Practical' / practical-heavy courses ('LH' in the code, usually 4 credits, e.g. S12BLH31, S13BLH21): CAE (theory) 50 + end-semester PRACTICAL exam 50. 'Theory + Project' / PBLA courses ('PB' in the code, or SISB4301 Universal Human Values; 3 credits): CAE 50 + project review/report 50. Regulations 2019 has no integrated type; theory and lab are separate courses.

variants.when: Professional Training / Internship / Interdisciplinary Project / Community Internship (2023)

project.notes: Project Phase I (3 credits) and Phase II (7 credits): reviews 50 + viva voce 50.

noncredit.notes: Mandatory Audit Courses (2023: SISB4151-SISB4155, e.g. Environmental Science and Engineering, Constitutional Law, Yoga) and Environmental Science and Engineering (2019: SBTA1101) carry 0 credits and never affect GPA/CGPA. 2023 grades them PASS/FAIL from internal assignments only. The 2023 annexure syllabus headers print 'Total Marks 100', and some 2019 editions print CAE/ESE 50/50 for SBTA1101; this does not matter for CGPA. NCC, NSS, YRC and sports appear as SATISFACTORY / NOT SATISFACTORY.

skillEnhancement.notes: 2023 Skill Enhancement Courses (SPCB..., SBAB4003-4005, VAC): 1 credit each in semesters 4, 5 and 6, ESE 100 only. They are credit-bearing and are assumed to be graded on the same bands (the regulations do not say otherwise).

rules: 1. If the code is in `courses`, use that entry. Everything below is a guess and the UI should mark it as an estimate the student can edit.

2. Regulation from the code: the letter after the programme code ('S' + 2 letters or 2-3 digits) is 'A' for 2019 and 'B' for 2023 (SCSA1201 is 2019, SCSB1303 is 2023, S11APT1 is 2019, S12BLH31 is 2023). Grading and pass rules are the same in both, so a wrong guess here does not change the grade.

3. Codes containing 'LH' after the B (S11BLH41, S13BLH21) are integrated practical-heavy theory, 4 credits (37 of the 38 catalogued LH codes; the exception S613LH71 is a 0-0-4-2 lab). Codes containing 'PB' (S11BPB51) are theory with project-based learning, 3 credits, CAE 50 + project 50.

4. Codes containing PROJ1 = Project Phase I (3 credits); PROJ2 = Project Phase II (7 credits, 15 for M.E.); PT1 = Professional Training I (2 credits); PT2 / IPROJ / CPROJ = PT II, interdisciplinary project or community internship (3 credits in 2023).

5. For a four-digit code (S + 2 letters + A/B + 4 digits), the first digit of the number usually gives the category: 1 = core theory (3 credits), 2 = laboratory (2 credits if the course maximum is 100, 1 credit if it is 50), 3 = professional elective theory (3 credits), 4 = open elective or humanities (3 credits; but SISB415x are 0-credit audit courses and SISB4301 is a 3-credit Theory+Project). This is an observed pattern, not a documented rule. M.E. codes use 5xxx (theory), 6xxx (lab) and 7xxx (electives).

6. ERP SubjectType 'THEORY' means theory, 3 credits. ERP 'Practical' does NOT mean a lab-only course: the ERP also labels practical-heavy (LH) and Theory+Project courses as Practical (S12BLH31, S13BLH21, SISB4301 in the real capture). Decide with rules 3-5 first; only a code with none of those markers that the ERP calls Practical should be treated as a lab.

7. Lab credits from marks: if the ERP's maximum for a lab is 50 (25 + 25), assume 1 credit (L-T-P 0-0-2); if it is 100, assume 2 credits (0-0-4). Five 2019 labs break this rule (1 credit, 100 marks), so this is only a guess.
8. Codes starting SISB415 (2023) and SBTA1101 (2019) are 0-credit audit courses: leave them out of the GPA.
fallback.notes: Credit counts in the catalog (regulation/type: credits/maxTotal -> count): 2019/noncredit: 0cr/50 x1; 2019/practical: 1cr/100 x5, 1cr/50 x7, 2cr/100 x57; 2019/project: 1cr/50 x2, 2cr/100 x9, 3cr/100 x19, 7cr/100 x9; 2019/theory: 2cr/100 x5, 3cr/100 x285, 4cr/100 x2; 2023/integrated: 3cr/100 x4, 4cr/100 x37; 2023/noncredit: 0cr/50 x5; 2023/practical: 1cr/50 x3, 2cr/100 x12; 2023/project: 2cr/100 x7, 3cr/100 x27, 7cr/100 x7; 2023/theory: 1cr/100 x14, 3cr/100 x263. Theory courses are 3 credits in 548 of 555 catalogued cases. 2019 exceptions: SAIC4001/SCCA9501 Industry 4.0 (2), SCSA1314/SCSA1315/SCSA1414 (2), and the earliest CSE 2019 edition's SCYA1101/SPHA1101 (4).

courseFieldNotes.subtype: theory | lab | practical-heavy | project-based-learning | project | professional-training | seminar | skill-enhancement | open-elective | mandatory-audit
courseFieldNotes.ltpc: L-T-P-C from the curriculum ('*' in T = a tutorial hour that is not counted in credits). For 2023 the extra EL (external learning hours) column is in `el`.
courseFieldNotes.semester: Semester in the first programme (`programme`) where the course appears; null for electives. The same code can sit in a different semester in another programme.
courseFieldNotes.maxTotal: internalMax + externalMax, from the curriculum CAE/ESE columns.
courseFieldNotes.source: The curriculum PDF the values were taken from. 'derived' is never used: every entry comes from a published table.
courseFieldNotes.conflicts: Present only where another official document disagrees.
